content.intended_use: Supply the mean-square consistency conclusion for the specified scalar Markov recursion.

proofs.locator: printed pp.401–405, Eq.(11)–(29),(36)–(42), Lemma 1–2 and Theorem 2
map: Printed pp.401–402, Eq.(11)–(18): define d_n=E[(x_n-theta)(M(x_n)-alpha)] and e_n=E[integral (y-alpha)^2 dH(y|x_n)]. Expand b_{n+1}-b_n=a_n^2 e_n-2a_n d_n. Monotonicity and M(theta)=alpha give d_n>=0, and bounded responses give 0<=e_n<=(C+|alpha|)^2. Summation shows sum a_n d_n<infinity and existence of b=lim b_n>=0.
Printed pp.402–403, Eq.(19)–(20), Lemma 1: if nonnegative k_n satisfy d_n>=k_n b_n and sum a_n k_n=infinity, the convergent series sum a_n k_n b_n together with existence of lim b_n forces b=0.

Printed p.403, Eq.(21)–(24): A_n=|x_1-theta|+(C+|alpha|)sum_{j<n}a_j bounds |x_n-theta| almost surely. For k_n=inf_{0<|x-theta|<=A_n}(M(x)-alpha)/(x-theta), integrate the pointwise inequality to obtain d_n>=k_n b_n.

Printed p.403, Eq.(25)–(29), Lemma 2: an eventual bound k_n>=K/A_n for some K>0, together with Eq.(26), gives sum a_n k_n=infinity. Eq.(26) entails sum a_n=infinity, so eventually A_n<=2(C+|alpha|)sum_{j<n}a_j.

Printed pp.404–405, Eq.(36)–(42): differentiability and positive slope give a neighborhood radius delta>0 with local secant ratio at least M'(theta)/2. On either side outside that neighborhood but inside A_n, monotonicity bounds the ratio below by delta M'(theta)/(2A_n). Eventually A_n>=delta; therefore Eq.(25) holds with K=delta M'(theta)/2. Apply Lemma 2 to conclude Theorem 2.

assumptions: There exists a single finite C>0 such that Pr(|Y(x)|<=C)=1 for every x in R, Eq.(4).
M is nondecreasing on all R, M(theta)=alpha, and the ordinary derivative M'(theta) exists as a finite real number with M'(theta)>0, Eq.(33)–(35).

The gain sequence is fixed, deterministic and strictly positive. It is of type 1/n in the paper's exact sense: 0<sum_{n=1}^infinity a_n^2<infinity, and sum_{n=2}^infinity a_n/(a_1+...+a_{n-1})=infinity, Eq.(6),(26).
Sampling follows the Markov construction Eq.(7)–(8); the statement is not a guarantee for arbitrary feedback laws specified only by an unconditional mean.
statement.conclusion: lim_{n->infinity} E[(x_n-theta)^2]=0, and hence x_n converges to theta in probability.
statement.objects_and_definitions: For each x in R let H(.|x) be the response distribution, M(x)=integral_R y dH(y|x). Let alpha,theta be finite real constants. From arbitrary deterministic x_1 in R define the nonstationary Markov chain by x_{n+1}=x_n+a_n(alpha-y_n), where the conditional response law at x_n is H(.|x_n). Set b_n=E[(x_n-theta)^2].
statement.parameter_domains: x_n,theta,alpha in R; n positive integers; C finite and positive; a_n>0. Positive constants c',c'' with c'/n<=a_n<=c''/n give a sufficient subclass, including a_n=a/n for every fixed a>0. The definition of type 1/n does not require these two-sided bounds.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every response model, finite root and target, fixed gain sequence and deterministic initial value satisfying these conditions, expectation is over the sequential responses of that model, and the conclusion holds as n tends to infinity.

summary: The original scalar recursion converges in mean square for every deterministic initialization and every fixed positive gain sequence of the paper's type 1/n, under uniformly bounded responses, nondecreasing mean and a positive derivative at the root.
title: Robbins–Monro Theorem 2: bounded-observation mean-square consistency
use_when: Establish asymptotic consistency of the original bounded-response scalar recursion; do not infer rates or bounded-variance-only applicability.
